title: US Data Center Gas Outlook 2035: On-Site Plants Boom | BloombergNEF
gist: Teaser executive summary of BNEF's US Data Center Gas Outlook 2035: natural gas supplies about 69% of power for new grid-connected data centers in BNEF scenarios, data center capacity rises from 47GW in 2025 to 194GW by 2035, power-sector gas burn grows 50%, and on-site gas plants add 2.9-3.4 Bcf/d of demand, making power the second-largest US gas demand growth driver after LNG exports.

themes.theme: Gas as the data center fuel

insights.claim: Natural gas will supply about 69% of the power needed by new grid-connected US data centers across BNEF's scenarios.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Data center buildout is fundamentally a gas demand story; supportive for US gas producers and gas turbine supply chains.

insights.claim: US installed data center power capacity is projected to reach 194GW by 2035, up from 47GW in 2025.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Roughly 4x growth in a decade frames the scale of power, gas and grid investment required.

insights.claim: BNEF expects power sector gas consumption in 2035 to be 50% higher than 2025 levels, making the power sector the second-largest driver of US natural gas demand growth through 2035, behind LNG exports, and increasing pressure on gas producers to scale supply.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Combined LNG export and data center pull tightens the US gas balance; bullish for upstream gas producers' volumes and pricing.
insights.locator: Data center power demand is projected

insights.claim: Data center developers seeking faster energization are turning to on-site gas generation, which BNEF estimates could add 2.9-3.4 Bcf/d of US gas demand by 2035.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF (free content)
insights.so_what: Grid interconnection delays push behind-the-meter gas, benefiting turbine/reciprocating-engine makers and pipeline operators serving data center sites.
